parts.t: Poplar covers North and South Poplar in Abbotsford, an area of farmland and homes south and southwest of the city. The name comes from five Lombardy poplars planted near King and Clearbrook Roads.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 12, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Abbotsford.
None of this is legal, planning or financial advice. If you are buying or selling, find out how the property is zoned, which schools cover the address, and what the community plan says.

blocks.text: What to look at in a Poplar property

parts.t: Poplar mixes farmland and homes, so the questions depend on what you are buying.

parts.t: No neighbourhood plan exists for Poplar itself. That leaves the ALR rules and the City’s Official Community Plan (OCP) to be applied property by property.
Abbotsford’s adopted neighbourhood plans cover only UDistrict, City Centre, Historic Downtown and McKee, so Poplar has no neighbourhood plan of its own.

Check whether others hold rules or rights over the land, such as covenants, rights of way and easements, and that includes any access you depend on.
On or near the land, any watercourse is worth raising with the City of Abbotsford, since rules about building near a stream can restrict where you build.
